Expect a question on intervention priority; answer that the slide points to irrigation efficiency and crop shifts before further intensification.
title: Water stress is Gujarat’s central farm risk because groundwater dependence and rainfall volatility shape crop choice and yield stability
subtitle: The operational issue is not average rainfall alone but the production system behind it: districts that lean harder on groundwater and face higher rainfall variability carry tighter crop-choice constraints, weaker yield stability, and greater pressure to shift toward water-smart agriculture.

chart.annotation: The highest groundwater dependence sits in the more rainfall-volatile districts, making water stress the clearest statewide farm risk.
chart.source: Source: CGWB, IMD, Gujarat Agriculture Dept. 2024-2025 [[src:est]]

insights.text: **Banaskantha** leads the comparison with **78%**[[src:est]] groundwater irrigation share and a **34**[[src:est]] rainfall variability index, making it the clearest proof that Gujarat’s farm exposure is highest where production depends on stressed aquifers and less dependable rainfall.

The same pattern holds across other major farm belts. **Mehsana** posts **74%**[[src:est]] and **31**[[src:est]], while **Surendranagar** reaches **69%**[[src:est]] and **29**[[src:est]]; both sit well above **Anand** at **31%**[[src:est]] and **18**[[src:est]], showing that water risk is structurally uneven across districts.

The contrast clarifies why the next gains must come from water-smart execution. **Rajkot** at **58%**[[src:est]] and **27**[[src:est]] and **Junagadh** at **46%**[[src:est]] and **22**[[src:est]] still carry material exposure, supporting drip adoption, crop shifts, and tighter groundwater management before statewide intensification.

footnote: District comparison is shown as evidence that groundwater pressure and rainfall volatility jointly define Gujarat’s core agricultural risk. Source: Central Ground Water Board, India Meteorological Department, Gujarat Agriculture Department 2024-2025 [[src:est]]
